notes.title: Devlog Update #3
notes.content: [h1]September 2025[/h1][p]Another month goes by we dedicated most of the time to finalizing the first iteration of the Campaign mechanics. At the same time we are updating our marketing material to boost visibility the following months. That said, let's talk about some specifics of the development process.[/p][p][/p][h2]Asset Pack[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45653284/aa9a0d1969f0b3bdff8cad4d543157d9788a2e5d.png"][/img][/p][p]So far, we’ve modeled and textured [b]over 400 assets[/b] that populate the different environments of the game world: from mountains, dense forests, bustling markets, villages, ancient temples, and all kinds of constructions, to the smallest props and ornaments. Combined, they give each location a unique and easily recognizable identity.[/p][p]From the start, our policy has been to prioritize performance above everything else. That means keeping assets low-poly and consolidating textures into just a handful of atlases. This approach not only ensures the game runs smoothly on lower hardware, but also allows us to focus development time on gameplay dynamics without creating optimization headaches down the road.[/p][p][/p][h2]Audience[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45653284/b20b1afed139abcc748dfc920f63a2f00a3fbf89.gif"][/img][/p][p]Keeping with our mandate of supporting low hardware specs, we set out to build an audience system that was both performant and visually engaging. Many games settle for cardboard cutouts, billboard sprites, or generic looping animations — but that didn’t fit our vision. We wanted the crowd to feel alive: reactive, dynamic, and unmistakably part of the game rather than just background dressing.[/p][p]From a technical standpoint, we combined [b]VAT (Vertex Animation Textures)[/b] with multiple atlases and color-replacement techniques to efficiently generate variety across the crowd. This let us render the entire audience in just a handful of draw calls. The process was surprisingly smooth thanks to the wealth of existing material on VATs.[/p][p]On the logic side, every audience member can be controlled individually. Their behavior adapts to match context: they cheer, boo, grow restless, and — at higher levels of discontent — even throw objects onto the field.[/p][p]We’re very happy with how it’s shaping up. Before release, we’ll continue refining the system to push the polish further, but the foundation is already strong: a lightweight audience that feels alive without tanking performance.[/p][p][/p][h2]Umpire Spotlight: Centurio[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45653284/5b8cc354cf96dfba6689f8202999643bc00b28a7.gif"][/img][/p][p]Feared and respected by locals and foreigners alike, the [b]Centurio[/b] marches with pomp, flanked by his escort, toward the grandstand of the stadiums where dozens of eager fans await the opening whistle. Like his fellow arbiters, he has been appointed by the [b]High Council[/b] to preside over the early phases of the Imperial Games — enforcing order with an iron will, dispensing justice on the field, and ultimately sealing the fate of the scoreboard.[/p][p]Yet the balance of judgment is rarely pure. With a watchful eye on the hidden wagers of the powerful and the volatile mood of the masses in the stands, the [b]Centurio[/b] often turns a blind eye to “unfortunate accidents” or “mysterious episodes” that disrupt the natural flow of play. When the clashes end — in triumph for some, in bitterness for others — he salutes the crowd with indifference and declares: [i]“Such is the will of the gods!”[/i][/p]

notes.title: Devlog Update #2
notes.content:
[h1]August 2025[/h1][p][/p][p]We're still deep in development on the campaign system and character design. The full game is finally taking shape, and it's satisfying to see ideas we mapped out over a year ago coming together at last.
Of course, being this our first game, there are a lot of hiccups here and there but every week brings us closer to something that feels cohesive and true to our original idea. 

As promised last month, let’s talk about the [b]characters[/b].[/p][p][/p][h2]The Characters[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45653284/3a5e76dd5d114e30235ee1b398e6cd75038d0d04.gif"][/img]
There will be hundreds of characters in the game, so we built internal tools to streamline their creation. Given our goal of [i]supporting a wide range of hardware[/i], we kept character models low in both polygon count and bone complexity.[/p][p][/p][p]Each character was designed based on the fantasy culture they belong to, their unique abilities, and their backstory within the world. We also created a variety of [b]armor sets[/b], organized into different tiers, to provide each character with the level of protection needed to withstand the constant collisions of this brutal sport—from simple headbands and hats to heavy, over-the-top helmets.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45653284/fd934d87a511d544b8cde2333d1338afbc4ed40e.gif"][/img]

Player characters [i]will evolve throughout the campaign[/i], improving their social status, unlocking better equipment, and enhancing their attributes as they climb the ranks of this unforgiving league.
[/p][p][/p][h2]The AI[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45653284/fa087061847b81bd370a585f1a97c17901971318.png"][/img][/p][p]We experimented with several approaches to AI. At first, it was just random actions. Surprisingly, this worked well enough for an MVP—it gave the illusion that the computer was “alive.” But as the project progressed, that obviously wasn’t enough. The AI needed to play well—and win.[/p][p]We initially tried [i]behavior trees[/i], even implemented our own version. But for a fast-paced action game, they were overkill. Too complex, too clunky. Not worth it.[/p][p]Eventually, we went with a [i]Utility AI model[/i]—very bare-bones. No need for fancy class hierarchies, nodes, or abstract structures. Just a clean set of well-organized script files.[/p][p][/p][h3]How It Works[/h3][p]Each player on a team has their own AI agent. [/p][p]Every AI cycle, the agent ranks all possible actions: shooting, attacking, blocking, repositioning, etc. It selects the top action for that frame—but crucially, it doesn’t execute it immediately. If all players acted at once, it would look robotic and unfair. No human could keep up.[/p][p]Instead, there's a team-level agent running on a slower cycle, roughly matching human reaction times. It looks at the best actions suggested by each player agent and decides which one to execute. This decision is influenced by multiple factors—player roles (e.g., goalkeeper actions take priority), the current match score, and more.[/p][p]Once an action is selected, it gets executed like a human would: by "selecting" the player and simulating input (press/release).[/p][h3]
Tuning Difficulty[/h3][p]We now have a lot of levers to tweak difficulty. We can shorten AI cycles, increase input responsiveness, or adjust action priorities. Want a defensive, aggressive, or chaotic team? It’s all doable. The system lets us give each team its own personality—and we’re still fine-tuning it.[/p][p][/p][h2]Highlight: Tristán[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45653284/4fe1b075a3c3f158fe22cb444ac69f0c8eb375f6.png"][/img]

Tristán was once a jester in the imperial court—more than just an entertainer, he had access to secrets, gossip, and the hidden machinery of power. Behind the painted smile was a sharp mind and a man who knew too much.[/p][p]But power is fragile, and court favor even more so. Tristán fell into disgrace under circumstances no one dares to speak of. Stripped of his rank, he was sent to the front lines to amuse tired soldiers in the mud and blood of the imperial war machine.[/p][p]He didn’t stay long.[/p][p]Tristán escaped, vanishing into the wilds where he lived among native tribes, learning their customs and stories. For a time, he found peace—or at least, a place to disappear. But fate wasn’t finished with him. Pirates raided the coast, capturing Tristán and selling him into slavery.[/p][p]Now, broken but unbowed, Tristán enters the arena not just to survive—but to reclaim control of his story.[/p][p]Despite his small stature and light build, Tristán’s years of hardship have made him remarkably resilient. He can absorb a surprising amount of punishment, making him especially effective in defensive roles where endurance and toughness matter more than brute strength.[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Devlog Update #1
notes.content:
[h1]July 2025[/h1][p][/p][h2]Current Progress[/h2][p]
We're kicking off a closed [b]playtest[/b] to validate the core mechanics, get a read on first impressions and the art direction. So far, the feedback has been sharp and constructive—exactly what we needed. We're in the middle of breaking it all down to prioritize improvements and cut what isn’t pulling its weight.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45653284/19e4f0c81bf82f20c6332e31115d8763531e8fc8.png"][/img][/p][p]On the development front, the [b]Campaign system[/b] is starting to take shape. This will bring everything together in a more cohesive way. We’re drafting the campaign map, building out save/load functionality, and creating a detailed match history log. The aim is to track every game played and surface as many relevant stats as possible— we want players to be able to see all the historic data, best scorers, set their own records and more![/p][p][/p][p]On the art side, we’re revisiting all player [b]characters[/b] and [b]equipment[/b]. Nothing to show just yet, but big changes are underway. We’ll have something solid to present next month—so stay tuned.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2]Highlight - City of Towers[/h2][p][/p][h2][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45653284/e5c4883d7339f0f15b2565af30fd68b546972b35.png"][/img][/h2][p]Deep in the Interian island[i], City of Towers [/i]stands as a twisted monument to both faith and spectacle. Once a sacred city, it was quickly repurposed by the Empire into a high-stakes arena. Boredom breeds rebellion, and nothing keeps the crowds obedient like a good match.[/p][p][i]Brabeutos[/i] are a constant presence here—part referee, part ringmaster—pulling levers and triggering secret mechanisms built into the arena walls. The dirt floor hides more than just bruised pride; behind those side doors, surprises await that can turn the tide of a match in seconds.[/p][p]The crowd? Fanatical!. They don’t cheer for finesse—they roar for ruthlessness and goals. If your team can’t deliver, [i]City of Towers[/i] will chew you up and spit you out.[/p][p]Are you ready to play their game?[/p][p]
[/p][p]
[/p]
